subject: Converge MAP: finalizing success criteria & exit gates
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <a.rivera@trialsystems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Converge MAP: finalizing success criteria & exit gates

Alex —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, attached is a first-pass MAP (MAP-v1.xlsx) that collates the success criteria, proposed exit gates, and a short list of acceptance tests we think validate both quality and operational readiness. High-level asks:

- Can you confirm the three items in the "Must pass" column (accuracy, throughput, reliability) are sufficient for your internal stakeholders?
- Are there additional telemetry signals your team requires for go/no-go (examples: sample-level recall checks, false-positive drift alerts)?
- Proposed close cadence: 4 weeks from pilot kickoff with a hard go/no-go checkpoint at week 3. Does Procurement need contract milestones aligned to that cadence?

Summary of proposed success criteria (short):
1) Functional: intent-level accuracy >= 92% on the 1k prompt set we shared (seeded edge cases included).
2) Performance: 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for 512-token requests under expected traffic profile.
3) Stability: zero incidents impacting >5% of requests during a 72h smoke window.
4) Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence items provided; data retention policy aligns to your retention window.

Exit gates (pass/fail):
- Pass: acceptance tests (A1-A6) pass and operator runbook validated in staging.
- Fail: any A1-A6 test that impacts functional correctness, or repeated SLA misses across two consecutive sampling windows.

Acceptance tests (short list):
- A1: End-to-end correctness vignettes (500 seeded prompts)
- A2: Latency under 1x/2x traffic profiles (load harness snapshot)
- A3: Cold-start/jitter check (5 cold restarts)
- A4: KV/prefix cache effectiveness (token-cost delta)
- A5: Security checklist verification (roles, audit logs)
- A6: Observability smoke (traceability from request to cost breakdown)

I copied Karthik and Marissa so they can confirm the SLO wording and the evidence artifacts we will publish. If the MAP looks good, we can lock the version and seed the acceptance tasks into the mutual-action plan this week.

Thanks —

Chloe Martin
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: MAP-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 sheets — Success criteria & Acceptance tests)

From: Alex Rivera <a.rivera@trialsystems.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@trialsystems.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 15:33:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Converge MAP: finalizing success criteria & exit gates

Chloe —

Appreciate the clear breakdown and the MAP draft. Quick responses inline: 

- Functional accuracy target: 92% is a reasonable start for pilot. Our clinical reviewers will want to push for 94% in production, but we're fine with a staged improvement plan. Can you add an explicit plan for how you'll measure the 1k prompt set (tooling + version of prompts)?

- Latency: 350ms at p95 is aggressive but desirable. Procurement will want a buffer in the SLA for sustained bursts. Can we specify a burst policy (e.g., 2min at 2x traffic) and fallback behavior (route to smaller model or rate-limit)?

- Stability: Agree on the 72h smoke window. For transparency, we also need a short list of required SOC2 artifacts (control IDs preferred) before legal signs off.

A couple of small asks from our side: 
1) Please enumerate the sample prompts (anonymized) you intend to use for A1 so we can sanity-check for patient PHI.
2) For A4 (KV/prefix cache), can you add an acceptance threshold for token-cost delta (e.g., <= 12% improvement over baseline)?

If you can update the MAP and evidence index, Procurement will coordinate a light term-sheet with milestones mapped to the 4-week cadence. We will loop Legal once SOC2 items are listed.

Thanks —

Alex Rivera
Director, Product Integrations
TrialSystems
a.rivera@trialsystems.com

Chloe / team —

Thanks for sending this. I made a few edits and uploaded the evidence index (evidence_index.pdf) that maps each acceptance test to an owner and artifact. Key clarifications I added: 

- Measurement plan for A1: we will run the seeded 1k against the same model version tagged in the MAP (v1.3-beta). We will provide a blinded report that shows per-intent precision/recall and edge-case breakdowns. Artifact: EVID-A1-2026-06 (report).
- A4 token-cost delta: set pass threshold to >=8% cost improvement OR <=5% token inflation on the top-10 heavy prompts. That gives us flexibility while still ensuring caching is effective.
- Latency fallback behavior: if sustained burst crosses 2x baseline for more than 2 minutes and p95 exceeds 550ms, we will automatically fall back to a pre-approved compatible model (variant B) and log an incident; this is a soft-fail gate but will trigger an engineer review.

Proposed timeline (mutual action plan milestones):
Week 0: Kickoff + evidence handoff (MAP locked)
Week 1: Staging acceptance runs (A1,A2,A6)
Week 2: Load testing + security artifact review (A3,A5)
Week 3: Production-canary smoke + runbook validation (A4)
Week 4: Review & go/no-go decision (final sign-off via DocuSign)

I added the following items to evidence_index.pdf and the HubSpot record: list of SOC2 control excerpts we will provide (control IDs: CC-3, CC-6, CC-8), a small checklist for anonymization proof, and the owner for each artifact (ops, sec, eng).

I'll update the MAP spreadsheet with these changes and attach in the HubSpot link. Chloe — if you can push the updated file to the shared link and flag the SOC2 excerpts for Legal, I'll coordinate the runbook owners and the canary window.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
